The University of Cincinnati Medical Center (UCMC) is Greater Cincinnati’s safety-net hospital and the region’s only adult academic medical center. UCMC has participated in the federal 340B Drug Pricing Program as a disproportionate share hospital since 1992. The program enables us to improve access to medications, reduce financial barriers for patients, and sustain essential health care services for vulnerable and underserved communities.
Each year, thousands of patients rely on UCMC for emergency, specialty, and complex care, regardless of their insurance status or ability to pay. Approximately 70% of patients treated at UCMC are covered by Medicare or Medicaid, establishing our essential role in caring for patients with significant medical and financial needs throughout Greater Cincinnati.
The 340B program allows eligible safety-net hospitals serving a disproportionate share of low-income patients to purchase certain outpatient medications at discounted prices. The resulting savings strengthen our ability to expand medication access, provide financial assistance, and preserve critical services that would otherwise require additional financial support.
A primary use of 340B savings is helping uninsured and underinsured patients obtain the medications they need. These savings support dedicated pharmacy personnel and medication-access programs that connect eligible patients with copayment assistance, manufacturer assistance programs, free or reduced-cost medications, and other financial support needed to begin or continue treatment. The savings also help ensure eligible patients leave the hospital with necessary medications following discharge, provide short-term medication supplies for behavioral health patients while follow-up care is arranged, and assist other vulnerable populations experiencing barriers to care.
In Fiscal Year 2025, the savings associated with UCMC’s participation in the 340B program helped strengthen our ability to support patient access, including:
•	Coordinate patient assistance for more than 7,000 individuals, connecting patients with free or low-cost medications.
•	Invest more than $1 million in the personnel and administrative infrastructure necessary to operate patient-assistance programs.
•	Maintain sliding-scale medication programs for patients being discharged from the hospital, including uninsured and underinsured individuals, and patients awaiting prior authorization. Facilitate $12 million in pharmacy copayment assistance for patients.
•	Provide more than $1 million in HIV drug therapy to individuals incarcerated at the Hamilton County Justice Center.
Beyond medication access, 340B savings helps UCMC sustain essential hospital-based and outpatient services relied upon by patients across the region. These services include the region’s only adult Level I Trauma Center, a verified adult Burn Center, Psychiatric Emergency Services, behavioral healthcare, maternal and infant care, and a broad range of primary and specialty care.
Savings from the program in 2025 also strengthened our ability to:
•	Provide subsidized dental care across more than 10,500 patient visits in 2025. 
•	Operate the Timonthy Freeman, MD, Center for Developmental Disabilities, Ohio’s only facility of its kind offering coordinated, wraparound services for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, which served more than 9,300 patient visits in 2025. 
•	Deploy the 513 Relief Bus to provide community-based health services, including blood pressure, diabetes, and cancer screenings, to more than 1,300 patients.
UCMC regularly evaluates community health needs through Community Health Needs Assessments, partnerships with community organizations, and ongoing engagement with the populations we serve. These efforts help inform how resources supported by the 340B program can be used to improve access to care, reduce health disparities, and respond to the evolving health needs of Greater Cincinnati.
The financial assistance policy at UCMC applies to eligible patients with household incomes of up to 400% of the federal poverty level and who meet other eligibility criteria. In FY 2025, UCMC alone delivered more than $278 million in community benefit, including more than $175 million in charity care and services for which reimbursement did not cover the cost of providing care.
By reducing medication costs and generating savings that can be reinvested in patient care, the 340B program strengthens UCMC’s ability to treat patients regardless of their ability to pay and helps sustain essential services that might otherwise require additional funding, be scaled back, or become unavailable.
